groups.title: The mother's voice
groups.q: The mother speaks warmly, sometimes scolding, like an ordinary woman from a small town. Does each line sound like her?

rows.text: How are you doing? Are you well? Feeling all right? Happy Norouz, Nana-pesar-jan.
Go outside too. Go where it's quiet.
– Baba what?
– The one with the silly teacher? Mm-hm, watch that one. It's funny. Laugh a little.
We all want to call and say he's been bothering us for thirty years, come take him away. If you agree too, we'll call.
– We're just joking around, Nana-pesar-jan. As if he'd ever go. If he did, it would be the answer to my prayers. By God. I swear on my own life.
– Gossip? It's gossip if they haven't done you wrong.
When he came back from Karbala, he'd put on a white glove. We walked all the way from the boulevard home, and he kept lifting his hand, as if his hand were something holy for people to kiss.
– Amir, is having the lead role a good thing?
– Ok, I'm not saying don't fall in love. First get to know the person, get married, and then if you want, fall in love. Then see if I say a word.
– I found you four times. Now come here, my good boy. Come take this and walk around inside the house.
– No. As long as this thread is in your hand, you won't get lost. The other end is in my hand. This way you won't get lost.
– Good, my clever boy. When something scares you, use a trick so you don't get scared.
– Where did such a wave come from?
– Ohhh my. Hmm, the countries must have been close to each other. When was the Bam earthquake?
– It's the end of days. Bibi's generation used to say that when the end of days comes, the earth keeps shaking.
– I vowed that if he gets better, I'll walk to Mashhad as a pilgrim.
– I mean, did you pass?
– Hmm, then I say my heart gets heavy too. Let me go see my friends.
Nana-pesar-jan, you really must make sure you eat well. Eat things that build you up. As long as you eat properly, I won't worry about anything else.
– At the hospital they kept calling out, "Family of Mrs. Adham!" Nobody moved. Then the nurse herself came over and said, "I think she's yours."
– He'd been drinking too much soda.
– Is this how you say thank you?
– Ugh, every time you ask him to get something, it's like he gets an electric shock.
– Goodness, Nini's suddenly feeling sleepy. I've been up since morning and haven't slept.

groups.title: Children's speech
groups.q: These lines are spoken by children. Does each one sound like a child?

rows.text: – This is even better than Stadio delle Alpi.
– Pfff, donkey, who knows better, the friend of the cousin of our brother-in-law's master craftsman who is the richest man in Tehran, or you, you calf?
– Sure, you come on the mission too, but you have to be really careful. The stages are really hard.
– Okay, put less. But not too much less. A little less.
– Stage three is an intersection. An intersection means really big. From this side all the way to that side. From this street to that street.
– If you get tired, don't come on the mission anymore.
– Lots of people fail here. They go left.
– The left side is dangerous. The house with the red door belongs to a really angry old man. Even angrier than Baba.
– Our school is at the end. The last house. If we make noise, the teacher will hit our hands with a ruler.
– On the other side of the school is the cemetery. It's really old. Some of the gravestones are gone. You can see the bones of the dead.
– Hey, why did you throw away the stick? What are we supposed to ring the doorbell with, then?
– You didn't say.
– Once she learns our names she'll like us.
